X vs Y — X, narrowly. X is the only one of the three that answered brief item 6's named sub-question and brief item 7 from artifacts rather than from prose: it grepped the tree for CC_LADDER and reported the exact two prose hits plus the five unrelated 'ladder' hits in scripts/handoff-fire.sh (:7238, :7242, :7848, :7855, :12701 — I reproduced all of it), it verified the Agent-only registration at settings-templates/settings.example.json:160, and it read migrations/0029 end to end (c10 at :2, the `grep -q 'frontier_fire_model'` precondition at :78, five config dirs at :86, and the post-write assertion at :121-125 that the Agent entry survived). Y left all four of those as explicit UNVERIFIED ('six guessed names returned does not exist'), so item 7 reduces to a doc restatement. Y wins back real ground — it caught the enforcer's own stale self-citation (hooks/frontier-spawn-gate.sh:27 → handoff-fire.sh:9303-9311, which is hf_inflight_key, verified), and it enumerated three uncounted shapes X missed entirely (dry-run as a whole-string glob, a quoted `--model \"fable\"` value, a different TMPDIR) — and X has one confirmed bad verification: it certified docs/research/opus55-utilization-2026-09-22/census/L1-census.md:62-63 as 'match[ing] exactly' when :62 says the cap refusal names `--model claude-opus-5` and line 138 says `--model opus` (grep count 0). On balance the two completed brief sections outweigh three bypass rows plus one bad certification, but only just.

X vs Z — Z, narrowly. Z carries everything Y had against X (M4/M5/M6 bypasses, the :27 self-citation) and adds verified findings X does not have anywhere: I ran the hook myself and confirmed Z's claims that a quoted launcher path and a `bash -c '…'` wrapper both escape :67 uncounted, that `--model \"claude-fable-5-1\"` escapes :75 uncounted, and — the sharpest one — that `cc-backlog add \"re-fire: handoff-fire.sh --model fable\"` DOES spend a slot, refuting the gate's own comment at :63-66. Z also produced the install.sh mechanism (merge gate :1232-1236, union skip on command-only at :1269, assert keyed on event|command with the matcher absent at :1292-1295), which I verified and which explains why the Bash arm is both un-addable and undetectable by the installer — a deeper answer to 'is it live' than X's template line, reached without opening the template. X's counterweights are real (the definitive CC_LADDER answer, the verified template line, the migration body, agent-teams-enforce.sh:366) but it also carries the L1-census false certification inside the very section about checking citations, a §1 sentence ('registered under two different PreToolUse matchers') its own §7 refutes, and it presents a 9-item bypass enumeration that omits the most ordinary spelling a human would type.
